walkthroughs.body_html:
Literature and Film Study — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Literature and Film Study brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Literature and Film Study.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which form is the correct imparfait of 'être' for 'il'?
options: est
était
fut
sera

mcqs.q: Which verbs take 'être' as their auxiliary in the passé composé?
options: When you don't know what tense to use.
Movement/state-change verbs (DR & MRS VAN DER TRAMP) and all reflexive verbs.
Just movement verbs - never reflexives.
All verbs take avoir.

mcqs.q: When do you use the imperfect rather than the passé composé?
options: For ongoing, habitual, or descriptive past actions.
Just for older events.
All verbs take avoir.
When you don't know what tense to use.

mcqs.q: How do you describe weather in the past, e.g. 'it was sunny'?
options: Present - 'Il fait beau'.
Passé composé - 'Il a fait beau' (which suggests a completed event).
Imperfect - 'Il faisait beau' (descriptive past state).
All verbs take avoir.
